subject: maths
title: Lines, Planes and Distances
welcome_lead: Equations of lines and planes in 3D, plus the distances between them.
meta_desc: HL Maths adventure on vector equations of lines, planes and distance formulas.
final_note: Line: r = a + λb; plane: r·n = d. Vectors rule 3D!

mcqs.q: What does n represent for a plane?
options: normal vector
point on plane
distance
direction along plane

mcqs.q: Is the result of 6 / 0.5 larger or smaller than 6?
options: Larger — dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger result (6 / 0.5 = 12).
Equal to 6, because 0.5 is half and so cancels out.
There are infinitely many roots.
Smaller, because division always makes numbers smaller.

mcqs.q: If the discriminant of a quadratic is negative, what does it tell you about real roots?
options: There is one repeated root — the curve just touches the x-axis.
There are infinitely many roots.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
There are no real roots — the graph does not cross the x-axis.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: There are infinitely many roots.
Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
